newsitem.title: IRAN: Aftershocks jolt Iran, quake toll rises to 554.
newsitem.headline: Aftershocks jolt Iran, quake toll rises to 554.

text.p: Two aftershocks on Sunday damaged property and caused panic among survivors of an earthquake that killed 554 people and made more than 35,000 homeless in mountainous northwest Iran, the official news agency IRNA said.

The aftershocks struck in the afternoon and measured about four on the Richter scale, weaker than the 5.5-Richter quake that devastated dozens of frozen-up villages around the provincial capital of Ardabil on Friday, IRNA said.
The tremors spread a wave of panic among survivors and caused damage to property, the agency said without giving details.
IRNA quoted Deputy Interior Minister Rasoul Zargar, who heads the relief operation, as saying earlier on Sunday that 554 people had been confirmed dead.
"Some bodies are still not dicovered...families have lost each other. We are not sure how people can be accounted for," a spokesman for Iran's Red Crescent told Reuters.
"A few more bodies may be lying undiscovered somewhere, but I do not think the death toll will exceed 554 by much," he said.
IRNA said 4,000 relief workers were setting up temporary settlements to help the survivors, who were given tents, blankets, heaters, bread, dates and canned fruit.
Rescue teams on Saturday completed searches that were hampered by cold weather to save victims of the tremor that injured 2,000 people, IRNA added.
Zargar told Iranian television on Saturday that 719 of the injured had been admitted to hospitals.
Snowfall on Sunday slowed relief efforts, an Iranian Red Crescent official said.

President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani called on authorities to bring speedy relief to stricken areas and urged people to send aid. Relief workers joined by residents set up 6,000 tents to shelter thousands of families, IRNA said.
Local authorities have announced three days of mourning in the province of Ardabil.

Friday's quake also jolted the town of Meshkinshahr and caused heavy damage to 110 villages. It occurred 16 hours after a strong tremor jolted Pakistan's Baluchistan province across Iran's southeastern border, killing about 60 people.

Ardabil, bordering the former Sovier republic of Azerbaijan, is an agricultural province inhabited mainly by Iran's Azeri minority. It is one of Iran's coldest regions with freezing temperatures during the winter.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in and around Bojnourd in northeast Iran.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in an area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
